name: Annapurna Base Camp
seoTitle: Annapurna Base Camp Solo Trek Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: Complete solo trekker's guide to Annapurna Base Camp. 10-day itinerary, permits, costs, safety and packing list. No guide required.

permits.name: ACAP
permits.notes: Bring passport + 2 passport photos. SAARC nationals pay $8. Pay in USD or NPR equivalent.

permits.name: TIMS
permits.where: Same office as ACAP — collect both at once
permits.notes: SAARC nationals pay $9. Cash only. Queue early (8am) in peak season.

itinerary.summary: First steps — river walk and village entry
itinerary.body: Take an early taxi to Nayapul (30 min from Pokhara). Collect TIMS stamp at Birethanti checkpoint. Gentle walk along the Modi Khola river through Gurung villages to Tikhedhunga. The famous Ulleri stone staircase starts here — rest tonight.
tips: Start before 9am to avoid midday heat
Last ATM is in Pokhara — withdraw NPR 40,000+

itinerary.summary: The Ulleri climb — hardest single day
itinerary.body: The Ulleri staircase is 3,000+ stone steps. Start at 6am, take it slow, take breaks at every teahouse. The reward is Ghorepani: Dhaulagiri views, good food, and your first taste of high altitude. Hydrate constantly — you gain 1,400m today.
tips: This is the hardest day — set the pace you'll sustain
First altitude night: avoid alcohol, drink 3L water minimum

itinerary.summary: Poon Hill sunrise then rhododendron descent
itinerary.body: Wake at 4:30am for the 45-min climb to Poon Hill (3,210m). On clear days: Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and Annapurna I all visible at once. After breakfast, descend through dense rhododendron forest (spectacular March–April) to Tadapani.
tips: Bring all layers — it's cold at the summit before dawn

itinerary.summary: Village descent to the sanctuary gateway
itinerary.body: Descend through forest to the Modi Khola valley, then a sharp climb to Chhomrong — the last major village before the sanctuary. Chhomrong is your last resupply point: buy snacks, top up cash, charge everything. Signal exists here (Ncell, weak). No signal after this.
tips: Critical stop — stock up on snacks, withdraw cash, charge devices
Leave a note at your hotel with your next destination

itinerary.summary: Into the gorge — bamboo forest and silence
itinerary.body: Steep descent from Chhomrong, then climb through increasingly dense bamboo and rhododendron forest. The gorge narrows and the trail becomes quieter. No signal from here. The Sinuwa junction has a fork — follow the GPX waypoint to stay on trail.
tips: No signal above Chhomrong — load offline maps now
Check GPX: the Sinuwa junction has a confusing fork

itinerary.summary: The gorge narrows — entering the sanctuary
itinerary.body: The gorge becomes spectacular: waterfalls, towering cliffs, and increasingly high peaks visible above. Himalaya Hotel area has 3 teahouses and is the last comfortable acclimatisation stop before the altitude zone starts at 3,000m+.
tips: If you have any AMS symptoms, stop here — do not push to Deurali tonight

itinerary.summary: Avalanche corridor and the high sanctuary
itinerary.body: IMPORTANT: The Himalaya Hotel–Deurali section passes through an active avalanche corridor. Leave by 6:30am, move quickly, do not linger. After Deurali (3,230m) the landscape opens to glacial moraine. MBC at 3,700m — you're in the high-altitude zone now. Drink constantly.
tips: Move through the avalanche section before 9am
Check SpO2 at MBC teahouse — if below 85%, rest a full day here

itinerary.body: Leave MBC by 6am. The approach reveals the full amphitheatre: Annapurna I (8,091m), Machhapuchhre (6,993m), Hiunchuli (6,441m) encircling you. Spend 2–3 hours at ABC — morning is clearest before clouds build. Descend to MBC for the night.
tips: If SpO2 drops below 80% at ABC, descend immediately — no overnight at 4,130m with AMS
The return to MBC is 1.5 hours — do it before cloud sets in

itinerary.body: Most trekkers return in 2 days. Day 9: descend to Chhomrong. Day 10: push through to Nayapul and taxi to Pokhara (arrive by 4pm). Trekking poles are essential on the Ulleri descent — the stone steps are harder going down on tired knees.
tips: Knees: poles mandatory for the Ulleri descent
Pokhara celebration dinner is a ritual — the Busy Bee and Caffe Concerto near Lakeside

gettingThere.intro: All roads lead to Pokhara. From there, it's a 30-minute drive to the trailhead.

steps.title: India → Kathmandu
steps.body: Fly direct from Delhi (2.5h), Mumbai (3h), Bangalore (3.5h). IndiGo, Air India, and Himalaya Airlines all operate this route. Book 3–4 weeks ahead for reasonable fares.

steps.title: Kathmandu → Pokhara
steps.body: Yeti/Shree Airlines domestic flight: 25 min, ~$70–100 one-way. Book in advance — sells out in peak season. Tourist bus alternative: ~$10, 6–7 hours.

steps.title: Pokhara → Trailhead
steps.body: Shared taxi to Nayapul: ~NPR 800. Private jeep to Kande (saves a day): ~NPR 1,200. Book from Pokhara Lakeside the evening before.

gettingThere.permitNote: Get ACAP + TIMS permits in Pokhara (ACAP office, Damside area) on your arrival day. Office opens 8am. Bring passport, 2 photos, and USD/NPR cash.

onTrail.note: Higher at altitude — this is average

safety.intro: ABC is well-trodden and generally safe. But altitude, weather, and solo logistics carry real risks. Know these before you go.

alerts.title: Avalanche corridor: Himalaya Hotel → Deurali
alerts.body: This section passes through an active avalanche zone. Move through early (before 9am), quickly, and do not linger. An April 2025 avalanche near Deurali killed a trekker. Do not take this lightly.

cards.title: Before you leave
items: Buy travel insurance with helicopter evacuation cover
Share your full itinerary with someone at home
Register at each ACAP checkpoint (they track you)
Download offline maps (OsmAnd or Gaia GPS)

cards.title: On the trail
items: Start trekking by 7am — afternoons cloud over
Never skip meals or water above 3,000m
Tell your teahouse your next day's plan
Carry a basic first aid kit and blister supplies

cards.title: Solo-specific
items: Buddy up informally with other trekkers for the Deurali stretch
Leave a note at each teahouse with your departure time
Carry a local SIM (Ncell/NTC) — some signal to Chhomrong
No signal above Chhomrong — plan accordingly

cards.title: Signs to descend immediately
items: Severe headache that won't respond to ibuprofen
Loss of coordination or balance
Confusion or disorientation
Persistent vomiting at altitude

items.name: Nepal SIM card (Ncell or NTC — buy at airport)

items: Print-ready PDF guide (all 10 days)
GPX waypoints for OsmAnd & Gaia GPS
Emergency contacts by altitude zone
ACAP + TIMS permit reference card

insurance.calloutHeading: Helicopter evacuation from ABC costs $3,000–5,000. Get covered before you go.
insurance.calloutBody: Travel insurance with helicopter rescue isn't optional above 3,000m. We recommend SafetyWing Nomad: covers emergency evacuation, hospitalisation, and trip interruption. From ~$50/month.

activities.title: Paragliding over Phewa Lake
activities.description: 30-min tandem flight with Annapurna views. The classic pre-trek experience.

activities.title: Sarangkot sunrise
activities.description: Jeep + short hike to the best Annapurna viewpoint. Do this the morning you leave for the trail.

activities.title: Phewa Lake boat + island temple
activities.description: Hire a rowing boat and visit Tal Barahi temple. 2 hours, deeply relaxing after a flight day.

activities.title: Pokhara old market walking tour
activities.description: Half-day walk through Lakeside and Old Bazar. Good for gear shopping orientation too.
